heroSubtitle: On May 17, 2026 — T-4 before the Helsingborg emergency NATO Foreign Ministers Meeting (May 21–22) — allied capitals are locked in their final pre-ministerial consultation phase. The central fault line: NATO Secretary General Rutte's 0.25% GDP Ukraine military pledge (~$143B/year combined) is facing resistance from France and the UK, while Baltic states, Poland, the Netherlands, and the Nordic allies push for adoption. If passed at Helsingborg, the pledge would be the first binding collective military aid commitment for a non-NATO-member state in alliance history — the financial architecture of 'NATO 3.0.' Rutte's pre-ministerial press conference is scheduled for May 20 at NATO HQ Brussels. Also May 17: European NATO allies' defense spending in purchasing power parity now exceeds the US (111%) — Defense News May 12. Congressional fallout continues from the Poland 2nd ABCT cancellation: Breaking Defense confirmed the Pentagon gave Army leadership 'just a couple of days' notice before the abrupt cancellation — a unit that had already cased colors, sent advance teams, and deployed equipment overseas. Background arc: May 15 — Army leaders grilled in Congress on ABCT cancellation; May 14–15 — Rubio 'what's the purpose of the alliance?' after Spain denied Iran war bases; May 14 — CNN confirms 10,200+ troop scope (Germany 5,000 + Poland ABCT 4,700 + missile battalion 500); May 13 — B9+Nordic Bucharest 'NATO 3.0' declaration + Rutte 0.25% pledge surfaced; May 12 — EU FAC Defence (Kallas 'red lines'); May 9 — Rasmussen 'disintegrating'; May 7 — 'terror incubators'; May 1 — Germany 5,000 withdrawal. Next: Rutte pre-ministerial brief May 20; Helsingborg FMM May 21–22; Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8, 2026.
